claims.explanation: Parachlorophenol is a phenolic antimicrobial that likely kills cancer cells through non-specific membrane disruption and oxidative stress rather than a single molecular target, so selectivity is probably driven by lineage-intrinsic metabolic and stress-response states. The pattern of sensitive lines (colorectal, NSCLC, squamous, melanoma, glioma) versus resistant lines (endometrial, thyroid, mesothelioma, some gastric) suggests that cells with high oxidative-stress vulnerability and active proliferation are most affected, while those with strong antioxidant or differentiation programs survive. Because no annotated target exists, the most predictive features are likely expression states of stress-response and phenolic-metabolism genes rather than individual driver mutations.

features.basis: KEAP1/NFE2L2 pathway activation confers antioxidant resistance to electrophilic phenols
Loss of KEAP1 activates NRF2 antioxidant program, protecting against phenolic oxidative stress
TP53-mutant lines dominate the sensitive set, consistent with impaired DNA-damage/oxidative-stress response
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, KYSE270) are among the most killed, suggesting oncogene-driven metabolic vulnerability
BRAF-mutant melanoma and colorectal lines appear in the sensitive group
PTEN loss in ZR751, KALS1, 786O, UACC62 may increase oxidative vulnerability via PI3K/AKT activation
KRAS-mutant colorectal, ovarian, pancreatic, and gastric lines are enriched in the sensitive set
CTNNB1-mutant endometrial and gastric lines are among the least affected
SF3B1-mutant lines appear in both sensitive and resistant sets, but resistant examples (UO31) suggest a possible protective association
ARID1A-mutant endometrial lines are resistant, possibly reflecting chromatin-state-dependent stress tolerance
KMT2D mutations appear frequently in resistant lines, suggesting altered epigenetic stress response
NF2-mutant pancreatic, ovarian, and thyroid lines are among the least affected
